title: Kiln scoring rules (protocol OPEN-05, section 3.3)
status: Proposed for freeze by the evaluation owner. Fixed and label-free: no value here was set or tuned on outcomes (OPEN-10 closed with no development-label path). Changing anything under "rules" changes rules_sha256 and requires changing FROZEN_RULES_SHA256 in src/kiln/scoring/score.py.

outcome.fix: No single verifier-accepted reaction energy (missing or conflicting). Obtain a cached_lookup reaction energy before acting on this pair; this category is the rule set's defined fallback, not a call from evidence.

A precursor reaches a sourced decomposition temperature, but its products have no decisive driving force to react with the other precursor. Choose a partner with a clearly negative reaction energy against the decomposition products, or a precursor that does not decompose at this temperature.

The computed reaction energy is above -50 meV/atom, within about two standard deviations of computed reaction-energy error, so there is no decisive driving force. Choose precursors with a more negative reaction energy (for example a more reactive or higher-energy precursor).

The furnace is below the Tammann temperature of both precursors, so neither lattice is expected to be mobile. Raise the furnace temperature above the lower Tammann temperature, or use a lower-melting precursor.

There is a driving force, but the furnace is below precursor A's Tammann temperature, so only precursor B is expected to be mobile. Raise the furnace temperature above both Tammann temperatures, or lengthen the dwell.

There is a driving force, but the furnace is below precursor B's Tammann temperature, so only precursor A is expected to be mobile. Raise the furnace temperature above both Tammann temperatures, or lengthen the dwell.

otherwise.fix: No change suggested: there is a decisive driving force and the furnace is at or above both precursors' Tammann temperatures (or a missing Tammann temperature was taken as neutral and flagged).

justification.reaction_energy_ev_per_atom: Thermodynamic driving force of the precursor pair, eV/atom, from Thermo's reaction_report (latest accepted estimate, so an escalated single_point or bounded_relaxation supersedes cached_lookup). When the Precursor agent has an accepted decomposition-aware energy (it requests decomposition_reeval only when the furnace is at or above a sourced decomposition temperature), that energy is used first, because the decomposition products are what react.
justification.reaction_energy_fallback: 0.0 eV/atom: a missing or conflicting reaction energy contributes nothing to p_react (neutral), raises a missing_evidence or conflict flag, and gives the 'insufficient_evidence' category through reaction_energy_present.
justification.driving_force_threshold_-0.05_ev_per_ato: Reaction energies at or above -50 meV/atom are not a decisive driving force. Hautier, Ong, Jain, Moore and Ceder, Phys. Rev. B 85, 155208 (2012), doi 10.1103/PhysRevB.85.155208: GGA+U errors on reactions forming ternary oxides from binary oxides are close to normal with a standard deviation of 24 meV/atom (rms 34.4 meV/atom), so 50 meV/atom is about two standard deviations. It is also the borderline band T_rxn proposed for Thermo's escalation rule (docs/escalation-rule.md).
justification.driving_force_weight_-20_per_ev_per_atom: One logit unit per 50 meV/atom of driving force, the same 50 meV/atom scale as the threshold. A scale convention, not a fitted value.
justification.tammann_comparison: Tammann's rule: solid-state reactivity becomes appreciable when the temperature reaches a fixed fraction of a reactant's absolute melting point (Merkle and Maier, 'On the Tammann-Rule', Z. anorg. allg. Chem. 631, 1163-1166 (2005), doi 10.1002/zaac.200400540). Kiln's Tammann temperatures are Kinetics' tool values (kiln.tools.tammann, 2/3 of the absolute melting point); this rule set compares them with the furnace setpoint at the natural threshold 0 degrees C: furnace below both Tammann temperatures is kinetically limited; below exactly one is partially reacted; at or above both is completely reacted.
justification.tammann_weight_0.005_per_c: One logit unit per 200 degrees C of furnace margin above each precursor's Tammann temperature (one per 100 degrees C on the mean margin). A scale convention, not a fitted value; it keeps the kinetic term comparable to the driving-force term over a few hundred degrees.
justification.tammann_fallback: 0 degrees C (furnace taken as at the Tammann temperature): a missing Tammann temperature contributes nothing to p_react, never triggers a kinetic cause, and raises a missing_evidence flag, so the call falls back to the driving-force evidence alone.
justification.decomposition: Precursor decomposition below the furnace temperature is read from what the Precursor agent emits: a decomposition-aware dE_ev_per_atom in its precursor_report exists only when the furnace is at or above a sourced decomposition temperature. If that energy is not a decisive driving force, the pair is 'transformed' (a precursor changed on its own but did not react). Unknown decomposition temperatures are flagged by kiln.review, not here.
justification.B60meV: Not used. Szymanski et al., Science Advances 10(27), 2024, doi 10.1126/sciadv.adp3309, found the first product to form predictable when its driving force exceeds every competing phase's by at least 60 meV/atom. That is a competition margin between products, which no specialist emits, and it is about which product forms first, not whether a pair reacts. It stays a regime marker in the baselines (OPEN-25) and is not a p_react input or category boundary here.
justification.p_react: A fixed-rule score in [0, 1] used for ranking (AUROC) and Brier. It is not a calibrated probability (AGENTS.md rule 10).
justification.changed_prediction: OPEN-17: a compute request changed the prediction when the provisional four-class category differs before and after it (kiln.scoring.score.changed_prediction).
